steps: Form a loose "C" handshape with each hand, fingertips curved and palms facing each other.
Raise both hands to the sides of your head, level with your temples.
Bring both hands down and inward toward your forehead in one smooth motion.
Finish with the C-hands resting at your temples, as if a wide-brimmed hat just settled onto your head.
tip: Think of the tricorn hats of colonial-era leaders — the C-hands trace the hat. The Deaf world also uses this sign for "superintendent."

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat and open in front of your chest, palm facing up.
Raise your dominant index finger near your cheek, fingertip pointed toward the open palm.
Flick the index finger quickly toward the palm and tap it once, as if spotting something.
Aim the flick in the direction of the person or thing you noticed, since the sign is directional.
Keep a bright, alert expression to match the suddenness of noticing something.
tip: This means notice / recognize / spot — as in "it caught my eye." Do not use it for a posted written notice; sign POST or INFORMATION for that.

steps: Make a cupped handshape with your dominant hand, fingers together and slightly bent.
Tap the fingertips lightly on the top of your head, palm facing down toward it.
Lift the hand a few inches straight up off your head in one short motion.
Keep the tap light and brief — the hand lands only once before lifting away.
tip: This is the body part only. For "head of an organization," sign LEAD or BOSS instead.

steps: Form an "A" fist with your dominant hand, thumb resting along the side of the fingers.
Thump your chest twice with the whole thumb-side of the fist, keeping contact soft and flat.
For YOURSELF, thrust the same "A" fist toward the other person with a slight jabbing motion.
Repeat the forward thrust once more, pulling back an inch between the two pushes.
tip: The thumb's side — not its tip — touches the chest. The sign also means "one's own" or "automatic," as in "on its own."

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of your chest with the palm facing up.
Bring the side of your dominant index finger down onto the center of that palm.
Repeat the downward tap at least once more with a quick, brisk motion.
Keep your face engaged and slightly animated, matching a lively back-and-forth conversation.
tip: Use repeated quick taps — a slow single tap would read as a different sign entirely.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of your chest with the palm facing up.
Touch the tip of your dominant index finger to the middle of that palm, palm-back.
Flip the index finger upward in one quick flick, like striking a match off the palm.
Freeze the finger pointing upward for a beat to mark a single, finished occurrence.
tip: Think of lighting a match — one quick upward flick means it happened exactly one time.

steps: Touch your forehead with the tip of your dominant index finger, palm facing left.
Bring both index fingers together side by side in the space in front of your chest.
Press the fingertips together briefly with palms facing each other and hold the contact.
Give a small firm nod of the head as you finish, to show mutual understanding.
tip: This is the compound THINK + SAME — "we are thinking the same thing."
